articles.title: Aprilia RSV4 Obscure Spe.Ed.: 500 Units, 220 hp (Nov 2026)
articles.excerpt: Aprilia showed the RSV4 Obscure Spe.Ed. at EICMA 2026: a numbered run of 500 with carbon wheels, Leg Wings, 220 hp and a 201 kg running weight.
blocks: Aprilia has presented the RSV4 Obscure Spe.Ed., a limited, numbered edition of 500 examples of its RSV4 superbike, at the EICMA motorcycle show in Milan. The Piaggio Group press release is dated 3 November 2026. The company says the bike keeps the RSV4's 220 hp V4 and is lighter than before, with a running weight of 201 kg, carbon fibre wheels and a pair of aerodynamic "Leg Wings" borrowed from its MotoGP prototype. As of 5 November 2026, neither source read for this article gives a price or an on-sale date.

In the Piaggio Group release, Aprilia calls the RSV4 "the world's most powerful production superbike" and describes the Obscure Spe.Ed. as built for track performance on technology developed by Aprilia Racing in MotoGP. The release says carbon fibre is used for much of the bodywork and for the wheels, bringing the weight to 201 kg in running order.

Fitting the full ART (Aprilia Racing Technology) exhaust and the carbon SC Project end can, both sold from Aprilia Racing's accessory catalogue, lowers the stated weight to 196 kg. Those parts are accessories, so the 196 kg figure is not the weight of the bike as it is shown.

Production: a numbered run of 500 examples
Engine: 1,099 cc V4, 220 hp at 13,000 rpm and 127 Nm at 10,800 rpm, according to the Italian outlet MotorBox
Weight: 201 kg in running order; 196 kg with the full ART exhaust and carbon end can (Aprilia)
Wheels: carbon fibre
Aerodynamics: carbon Leg Wings, described by Aprilia as new to the class
Suspension: mechanically adjustable Öhlins, a TTX shock and a NIX fork
Finish: all black, with the name and serial number laser-engraved on the steering plate, according to MotorBox

Aprilia says the Leg Wings are already used on its RS-GP MotoGP prototype and are meant to create downforce without hurting handling. The release says the carbon wings are part of an aerodynamic package developed in the wind tunnel. MotorBox adds that they raise rear downforce by 20 percent and that the seat and passenger pegs are removable. That 20 percent figure appears in the MotorBox article only, not in the press release text read for this article.

Aprilia states that the Obscure Spe.Ed. brings Leg Wings to the superbike class for the first time. This article reports that as the company's statement and has not checked it against other makers' bikes.
How it differs from the RSV4 Factory

MotorBox says the Obscure is 3 kg lighter than the RSV4 Factory and that its carbon wheels are more than 2 kg lighter than the Factory's aluminium ones. On suspension, the release says Aprilia chose mechanically adjustable Öhlins units because they suit the "customisation requirements" of riders during races.

According to MotorBox, the bike has a six-axis IMU, ride-by-wire throttle, six riding modes (three road, three track), cornering ABS, the APRC package with traction and wheelie control, an electronic quickshifter, and the Track Pack and Race Pack. MotorBox also says it is homologated for road use. These details come from that article and not from the press release text read here.
Not yet announced in the sources read: price, on-sale date and markets, including India. Any figures quoted elsewhere before Aprilia publishes them should be treated as unconfirmed.

The same Piaggio Group release lists other Aprilia items at EICMA 2026: an RS 660 Phillip Island Tribute special edition, a new SXR 125 entry scooter, updated SR GT 125 and 200 scooters, and new 2027 graphics for the Factory models called aPRC Backbone, a red-on-black design inspired by the electronic signals in Aprilia's control system.
This article is dated 5 November 2026 and is not updated afterwards. Check Aprilia's own website for prices and availability.

articles.title: Aprilia SR GT 125 and 200 Updated at EICMA (Nov 2026)
articles.excerpt: Aprilia updated its SR GT 125 and 200 urban adventure scooters at EICMA 2026 with a 5-inch TFT display, USB-C, a full-face helmet space and new colours.
blocks: Aprilia has shown updated versions of its SR GT 125 and SR GT 200 "urban adventure" scooters at the EICMA show in Milan. The Piaggio Group announced them in a press release dated 3 November 2026. The changes are mostly equipment: a 5-inch colour TFT display, a USB-C port as standard, an under-seat space that now takes a full-face helmet, and new colours. As of 5 November 2026, neither source read for this article gives a price or an on-sale date.

Aprilia describes the SR GT as a family of scooters with long-travel suspension and more ground clearance than a typical city scooter, with enduro-inspired features meant for rougher roads and tracks. The release says the restyling improves practicality and gives the scooters a fuller equipment package.

Display: a new 5-inch colour TFT with more readings and easier reading, according to Aprilia
Connectivity: ready to connect to a smartphone for pictogram navigation through the Aprilia MIA module, which is an accessory
Charging: a USB-C port as standard
Storage: the under-seat compartment now fits a full-face helmet
Controls: new handlebar switchgear, reported by the Italian outlet MotorBox
Wheels: a new design inspired by the larger SR GT 400, reported by MotorBox
The press release gives these output figures for the two engines. MotorBox calls them i-get engines with a Start and Stop function.

SR GT 125: 11 kW at 9,000 rpm and 12 Nm of torque at 6,750 rpm
SR GT 200: 13 kW at 8,650 rpm and 16.5 Nm of torque at 7,000 rpm

Aprilia says the 125 version now reaches a higher top speed because of improved calibration of the final drive, the part that carries power to the rear wheel. The company does not give the new top speed in the release text read for this article. MotorBox converts the outputs to about 15 hp for the 125 and 17.6 hp for the 200.

MotorBox lists the standard colours as Opalescent Light, Aprilia Black and a new Boulder Grey. It also reports a more sporty SR GT Sport version in Red Raceway, Boulder Grey and Tornado Green, with a two-tone black and red seat and dark details. Colour names for the Indian market, if the scooters are sold there, have not been published.

Prices in any market
On-sale dates
Whether and when the updated scooters will be sold in India
The 125's new top speed

The press release was one item in a longer Piaggio Group announcement that also covered the Aprilia RSV4 Obscure Spe.Ed., a new SXR 125 entry scooter, and updated Beverly, Medley and Typhoon scooters.
This article is dated 5 November 2026 and is not updated afterwards. Check Aprilia's website or a dealer for current prices, availability and specifications.

articles.title: Yamaha Ténéré 4 Concept Shown in Milan (Nov 2026)
articles.excerpt: Yamaha showed the Ténéré 4 Concept in Milan on 2 November 2026: a light A2 adventure bike with a new single-cylinder engine. No power, price or date yet.
blocks: Yamaha Motor Europe showed the Ténéré 4 Concept in Milan on the evening of 2 November 2026, the day before the EICMA show opened its press days. It is a light adventure motorcycle for riders on an A2 licence, with a newly developed single-cylinder engine and a new frame. It is a concept, not a production model. Yamaha has not given engine size, power, weight, price or a launch date. Yamaha's own press release could not be opened for this article, so the details below come from two independent outlets that reported on it.

Yamaha presented the bike at an event it called "Redefine the Standard". In the days before, many riders had guessed it would be a Ténéré 900. It was not. The Ténéré name has so far belonged to Yamaha's twin-cylinder Ténéré 700, and the new bike is a smaller sibling below it.

According to MOTORCYCLES.NEWS, Yamaha describes the concept as part of a development project for a light, agile adventure bike that can be ridden on an A2 licence. The same report says strong customer demand prompted the project and that Yamaha plans to keep expanding its adventure range in the coming years.

Engine: a completely new single-cylinder engine, with no displacement or power given
Frame: a new frame, described as stable and light
Suspension: KYB components front and rear
Wheels: spoked, 21 inches at the front and 18 inches at the rear
Tyres: Michelin Anakee Wild
Exhaust: a compact titanium system from Akrapovič
Look: a flat, low tank and slim lines that echo the Ténéré 700; the concept carries a contour-line graphic in grey, black and blue with gold fork tubes
The Italian outlet MotorBox, which also covered the reveal, lists the same engine, frame, suspension, wheels, tyres and exhaust, and adds that Yamaha's announcement "gives no numbers" for the bike.
What Yamaha says the engine is meant to do

Yamaha's stated aims for the engine, as reported by MOTORCYCLES.NEWS, are efficient fuel burn, strong pull at low and middle revs, and usable power at high revs. Strong low-rev pull matters off-road because it lets a rider control the bike cleanly at slow speed. The frame is meant to give stability and good handling on both tarmac and difficult trails.

The A2 licence is a European category for riders stepping up from smaller bikes. It limits motorcycle output, so makers build A2 versions of their models. Yamaha has not said what output the Ténéré 4 would have.

Engine capacity and power
Weight
Price
Whether and when it becomes a production bike
Markets where it would be sold
A concept can change before production, or may never be built. MOTORCYCLES.NEWS also mentions an unconfirmed report from France about the bike; since it is unconfirmed, nothing from it is used here.
This article is dated 5 November 2026 and is not updated afterwards. Check Yamaha's own website for any announcement that follows.

articles.title: What an NPU Is and Why New Laptops and Phones Have One
articles.excerpt: A neural processing unit, or NPU, is a chip block built to run AI models efficiently. Here is what it does, how TOPS is measured and how it differs from a CPU or GPU.
blocks: A neural processing unit, or NPU, is a part of a chip designed to run artificial intelligence workloads quickly and with little power. It does one family of calculations, the matrix maths behind neural networks, rather than everything a processor might be asked to do. Phones have carried such blocks for years, and laptops now advertise them too. This article explains what an NPU does, what "TOPS" means on a spec sheet, and where an NPU fits next to the CPU and GPU.

Wikipedia defines an NPU, also called an AI accelerator or deep learning processor, as a class of specialised hardware designed to speed up artificial intelligence and machine learning applications, including neural networks and computer vision. An NPU can be a separate chip, or a block inside a CPU or a graphics processor. Microsoft describes it as a specialised chip for AI-heavy tasks such as real-time translation and image generation.

The aim is usually inference, which means running an AI model that has already been trained. Training a large model takes far more hardware, usually in data centres. Running a small trained model, for example to blur a video call background, is the job an NPU in a laptop or phone is built for.
Why not just use the CPU or GPU?

A CPU is built for general work: running programs, making decisions, handling many different tasks. A GPU has many small units that do similar sums in parallel, which suits graphics and also AI. An NPU narrows the job further. Wikipedia says NPUs focus on low-precision arithmetic and are often designed with many cores and special data-flow layouts. Because they do less, they can use less energy for the same AI work.

Microsoft says the NPU on a Windows Copilot+ PC can process large amounts of data in parallel and use energy on AI tasks more efficiently than a CPU or GPU, which helps battery life. Windows decides which part of the chip should do each task, and the NPU needs software written to use it. An app that is not written for the NPU will not run faster just because the chip is present.

Computers store numbers with different amounts of detail. A scientific calculation may need many digits. Many trained AI models work well with far fewer. Wikipedia notes that consumer NPUs are designed for low-bitwidth operations using number types such as INT4, INT8, FP8 and FP16. Fewer bits per number means less data to move and smaller circuits, so more of the sums fit into the same space and power budget.

The common speed rating for an NPU is TOPS, trillions of operations per second. Wikipedia explains that TOPS does not say exactly which kind of operation is counted, and that it is typically INT8 additions and multiplications. That means two chips with the same TOPS number can behave differently, and the figure should not be compared with a CPU's clock speed or a GPU's teraflops.

Microsoft sets a number for its own branding: it says many new Windows AI features need an NPU that can run at 40 or more TOPS, and it describes Copilot+ PCs as having an NPU that can perform more than 40 trillion operations per second. As of the version of Microsoft's page read for this article, the listed examples include chips from Qualcomm, AMD and Intel.

Phones: Wikipedia lists AI accelerators in Apple silicon, Qualcomm, Samsung, Huawei and Google Tensor phone processors
Laptops: Wikipedia says NPUs were added to Intel processors from about 2022 and AMD processors, after Apple added one around 2017
Data centres: Google's TPU and Amazon's Trainium and Inferentia chips are accelerators of a larger kind
Vision devices: Wikipedia notes vision processing units are used in drones and augmented-reality headsets

Programs do not talk to an NPU directly. They use a framework such as Core ML on Apple devices, DirectML or Windows ML on Windows, or LiteRT on Android, which Wikipedia lists as ways to reach these chips. Microsoft says Windows ML detects the available hardware and downloads the matching components, so a developer does not need to bundle each vendor's code. Trained models are often shared in formats such as ONNX.

An NPU runs trained AI models efficiently; it is not a faster general processor
TOPS is a rough guide, and it counts a specific kind of low-precision operation
Benefits depend on software written to use the NPU
Cloud AI services still run on data-centre hardware, not on the NPU in a laptop
General information only. Specification figures differ between chip generations and makers; check a product's own specification page before buying.

sources.title: Copilot+ PCs developer guide, Microsoft Learn

articles.title: How a Battery Electric Car Works: Motor, Pack, Charger
articles.excerpt: A battery electric car swaps the engine, fuel tank and gearbox for a battery pack, power electronics and a motor. This guide names each part and what it does.
blocks: A battery electric vehicle, or BEV, gets all its drive energy from a battery pack on board and moves with one or more electric motors. There is no engine, no fuel tank and no exhaust. This guide goes through the main parts of a BEV's drivetrain, following the energy from the plug to the wheels, using the descriptions published by the US Department of Energy's Alternative Fuels Data Center and by Wikipedia.
What counts as a battery electric vehicle

Wikipedia defines a BEV as a vehicle that uses electrical energy only from an on-board battery pack to power its traction motors. That leaves out hybrids, which add an internal combustion engine, and fuel cell vehicles and range-extended electric vehicles, which burn or consume fuel to make electricity. A BEV refills by plugging into a charging station or the grid, or in some designs by swapping in a charged battery.
From the plug to the pack
Three parts handle charging, according to the Energy Department's description.

Charge port: the socket that connects the car to an external power supply
Onboard charger: takes the incoming AC electricity from the charge port and converts it to DC to charge the battery; it also talks to the charging equipment and watches voltage, current, temperature and state of charge
Traction battery pack: stores the electricity used by the drive motor
Fast chargers deliver DC directly. The onboard charger is the part that matters when you plug into ordinary AC supply.
From the pack to the wheels

Power electronics controller: manages the flow of electricity from the battery and controls the speed of the motor and the torque it produces
Electric traction motor: uses the battery's power to turn the wheels; some vehicles use motor-generators that both drive and regenerate
Electric transmission: passes mechanical power from the motor to the wheels

The controller is how the driver's pedal input becomes motion. Wikipedia notes that BEVs use motor controllers to vary output power and torque, which removes the need for clutches, multi-gear transmissions and sophisticated engine cooling that conventional engines need.
The small parts that still matter

DC/DC converter: changes the battery's high-voltage DC to the lower voltage that runs lights, screens and other accessories, and recharges the auxiliary battery
Auxiliary battery: provides electricity for vehicle accessories, much like the 12-volt battery in a petrol car
Thermal system: keeps the motor, power electronics, battery and other parts in a proper temperature range

A conventional car has a radiator because an engine wastes a lot of energy as heat. An electric drivetrain wastes less, but batteries and power electronics still have a working temperature range, which is the job of the cooling system.
Why efficiency differs from a petrol car

Wikipedia compares energy density. Modern lithium-ion batteries store 0.9 to 2.63 megajoules per litre, against 34.2 megajoules per litre for petrol, so a battery holds far less energy for its volume. The article says this is partly offset by the high conversion efficiency of electric motors, and states that BEVs travel roughly three times further than similar-size combustion vehicles per megajoule of stored energy. That comparison is a general figure; real results depend on the vehicle and use.

Hybrid: a combustion engine works alongside electric motors
Plug-in hybrid: a hybrid whose battery can be charged from the grid
Range-extended electric vehicle: an engine-driven generator makes electricity
Fuel cell electric vehicle: a fuel cell makes electricity from fuel
General information only. Charging speeds, range and battery warranties differ between models, so use the manufacturer's own figures for any specific car.

sources.title: How Do All-Electric Cars Work?, Alternative Fuels Data Center, US Department of Energy
